extracted.intended_audience: Federal agency officials (liaison, certifying, authorizing officers) preparing and submitting documents to the Office of the Federal Register; drafters of rules, notices, executive orders, proclamations, and Government Manual statements
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and standards for preparing, formatting, certifying, routing, filing, scheduling, and codifying agency documents for the Federal Register and the U.S. Government Manual, including emergency/deferred handling and Executive Order/proclamation routing. Covers required copies, signatures, preamble structure, style, and indexing terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of agency representatives (§16.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall designate, from its officers or employees, persons to serve as a liaison officer and alternate; a certifying officer and alternate; and an authorizing officer and alternate. The same person may be designated to serve in one or more of these positions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agency must notify the Director of the name, title, address, and telephone number of each person designated and promptly notify the Director of any changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liaison officer selection and notification (§16.1 & §16.2(b),(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: In choosing its liaison officer, each agency should consider that this officer will be the main contact between the agency and the Office of the Federal Register and should be directly involved in the agency’s regulatory program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies shall notify the Director of the liaison officer's contact details and promptly update any changes. The liaison will carry out duties set forth in §16.2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liaison duties (§16.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency liaison officer shall represent the agency in all matters relating to the submission of documents to the Office of the Federal Register and respect general compliance with this chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional liaison duties: be responsible for effective distribution and use within the agency of Federal Register information on document drafting and publication assistance (§15.10), promote agency participation in technical instruction authorized by §15.10, and be available to discuss submitted documents with FEDERAL REGISTER editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certifying officer duties (§16.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency certifying officer is responsible for attaching the required number of true copies of each original document submitted by the agency and for making the certification required by §§18.5 and 18.6.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorizing officer responsibilities (cross-references §16.1, §17.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency authorizing officer is designated to serve with relation to the Office of the Federal Register and has responsibilities related to document authorization and distribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically, the agency authorizing officer is responsible for furnishing to the Director a current mailing list of officers or employees authorized to receive the FEDERAL REGISTER, the Code of Federal Regulations, and the Weekly Compilation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Receipt and processing hours (§17.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless special arrangements are made, the Office of the Federal Register receives documents only during official working hours and holds each document for confidential processing until it is filed for public inspection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regular schedule filing procedure and timing (§17.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each document received shall be filed for public inspection only after it has been received, processed and assigned a publication date. Documents received by 2:00 p.m. that meet requirements are assigned to the regular schedule; those received after 2:00 p.m. are assigned to the next working day’s regular schedule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regular schedule mapping (received → filed → published): Mon before 2pm → Wed filed → Thu published; Tue → Thu → Fri; Wed → Fri → Mon; Thu → Mon → Tue; Fri → Tue → Wed. Legal Federal holidays add one work day. Except as provided in paragraph (d), receipt by 2:00 p.m. is considered a request for regular schedule filing and publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government in the Sunshine Act notices timing (§17.2(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Each notice of meeting issued under the Government in the Sunshine Act (5 U.S.C. 552b(e)(3)) is placed on immediate public inspection after it has been received, processed, and assigned a publication date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notices received before 4:00 p.m. are scheduled to be published 2 working days later; notices received after 4:00 p.m. are scheduled to be published 3 working days later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency publication criteria (§17.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: The emergency schedule is designed to provide the fastest possible publication of a document involving the prevention, alleviation, control, or relief of an emergency situation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency publication procedure and timing (§17.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency requesting publication on the emergency schedule shall briefly describe the emergency and the benefits of immediate publication in the FEDERAL REGISTER; the request must be made by letter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director assigns a document to the emergency schedule whenever the Director concurs with a request and it is feasible; each document assigned to the emergency schedule shall be published as soon as possible and will be filed for public inspection on the working day before publication unless emergency filing is also requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for emergency filing for public inspection (§17.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency may request emergency filing for public inspection for documents to be published under the regular, emergency, or deferred publication schedules to provide the fastest public access after receipt, processing, and assignment of a publication date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emergency filing is considered a special arrangement under §17.2 that deviates from the regular schedule. A document receiving emergency filing remains on public inspection until it is published according to the publication schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure and timing for emergency filing for public inspection (§17.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency requesting emergency filing shall briefly describe the emergency and benefits to immediate public access in a letter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director shall approve an emergency filing request whenever the Director concurs and it is feasible; each document approved shall be filed as soon as possible following processing and scheduling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deferred publication schedule criteria (§17.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: A document may be assigned to the deferred schedule if there are technical problems, unusual or lengthy tables or illustrations, or the document is of such size as to require extraordinary processing time, or if the agency requests a deferred publication date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office of the Federal Register staff will notify the agency if documents must be assigned to the deferred schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originals and copies required (§18.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as provided for Executive orders and proclamations (§19.2), each agency submitting a document to be filed and published shall send an original and two duplicate originals or certified copies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the document is printed or processed on both sides, one of the copies sent must be a collated, single-sided copy. Agencies with computer-processed data are urged to consult OFR staff about possible use of the data in the publication process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on combined-category documents (§18.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director will not accept a document for filing and publication if it combines material that must appear under more than one category in the FEDERAL REGISTER (e.g., combining rulemaking and notice of proposed rulemaking material).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When two related documents are to be published in the same issue, the agency may insert cross-references in each document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission of documents and letters of transmittal (§18.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each document authorized or required by law to be filed for public inspection and published shall be sent to the Director of the Federal Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Except for cases requiring special handling, there is no need for a letter of transmittal. Receipt dates are determined when a signed original and clear and legible copies are received.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of document: physical requirements and unacceptable forms (§18.4(a),(b),(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: A printed or processed document may be accepted if it is on bond or similar quality paper, legible, and free of adhesive or correction tape. A document in the form of a letter or press release may not be accepted for filing/publication in rules and regulations, proposed rules, or notices categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original documents submitted by telecommunication and authenticated by digital signatures consistent with applicable Federal standards and OFR technical specifications may be accepted for publication. Telecommunication submission currently limited to selected pilot projects; agencies with computer processed data are urged to consult OFR staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certified copies requirements (§18.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certified copies or duplicate originals of each document must be submitted with the original, and each copy or duplicate must be entirely clear and legible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of certification (§18.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each copy of each document submitted for filing and publication (except a Presidential document or duplicate original) must bear the certification: '(Certified to be a true copy of the original)'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The certification must be signed by a certifying officer designated under §16.1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature requirements (§18.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: The original and each duplicate original document must be signed in ink, with the name and title of the official signing the document typed or stamped beneath the signature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initialed or impressed signatures will not be accepted. Documents submitted under §18.4(c) (digitally authenticated) may be accepted as authenticated by digital signatures consistent with applicable federal standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of seal (§18.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of a seal on an original document or certified copy is optional with the issuing agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Style conformity (§18.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each document submitted for filing and publication shall conform to the current edition of the U.S. Government Printing Office Style Manual in punctuation, capitalization, spelling, and other matters of style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illustrations, tabular material, and forms (§18.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: If it is necessary to publish a form or illustration, a clear and legible original or a clear and completely legible reproduction approximately 8 1/2 by 11 inches shall be included in the original document and each certified copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A document that includes tabular material may be assigned to the deferred publication schedule (see §17.7).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preamble requirements and format (§18.12)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency submitting a proposed or final rule must prepare a preamble to inform a non-expert reader of the basis and purpose for the rule/proposal. The preamble shall contain the following items in the specified format: AGENCY; ACTION; SUMMARY; DATES; ADDRESSES; FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT; SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SUMMARY must be brief statements, in simple language, of: (i) the action being taken; (ii) the circumstances which created the need for the action; and (iii) the intended effect of the action. DATES should specify comment deadlines, effective dates, hearing dates, etc., as applicable. The agency may include in SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION (as applicable): background and major issues; significant differences between final and proposed rule; response to substantive public comments; and any other information the agency considers appropriate. The list of index terms required by §18.20 shall be placed as the last item in the Supplementary Information portion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal or correction of filed documents (§18.13)
rubrics_metrics.description: A document filed for public inspection but not yet published may be withdrawn or corrected by the submitting agency. Withdrawals or minor corrections may be made with a timely letter signed by an authorized representative; extensive corrections may require withdrawal of the document from publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both the originally filed document and the withdrawing or correcting letter shall remain on file and will be retained after the public inspection period expires.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of printing errors in the Federal Register (§18.15)
rubrics_metrics.description: The FEDERAL REGISTER may be corrected by insertion of an appropriate notation or reprinting without further agency documentation if the Director determines that the error would tend to confuse or mislead the reader or affect text subject to codification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The issuing agency shall review published documents and notify the Office of the Federal Register of printing errors found. If the error was in the document as submitted by the agency, the issuing agency must prepare and submit a correction document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement of expired regulations (§18.16)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies may reinstate regulations removed from the CFR data base which have expired by their own terms only by republishing the regulations in full text in the FEDERAL REGISTER.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective dates and time periods (§18.17)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each document submitted that includes an effective date or time period should either set forth a date certain or a time period measured by a certain number of days after publication in the FEDERAL REGISTER. When measured by days after publication, Office of the Federal Register staff will compute the date to be inserted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Computation rules: count the day after publication as one and count each succeeding day including Saturdays, Sundays, and holidays; if final count falls on a Saturday, Sunday, or holiday, the date certain will be the next succeeding Federal business day. If an effective date depends on Congressional action or court decision that changes the effective date, the issuing agency shall promptly publish a document announcing the effective date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of subjects in agency regulations (§18.20)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency submitting a document published in Rules and Regulations or Proposed Rules shall include a list of index terms for each CFR part affected by the document and place the list of index terms as the last item in the Supplementary Information portion of the preamble.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To prepare the list of index terms, agencies shall use terms from the Federal Register Thesaurus of Indexing Terms. Agencies may include additional terms not in the Thesaurus so long as appropriate Thesaurus terms are also used. Copies of the Thesaurus are available from the Office of the Federal Register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form requirements for Executive orders and proclamations (§19.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed Executive orders and proclamations shall be prepared with a suitable title, a citation of the authority under which issued, and conform generally to the most recent edition of the U.S. Government Printing Office Style Manual in punctuation, capitalization, spelling, and other matters of style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional requirements: spelling of geographic names shall conform to Board on Geographic Names decisions; land descriptions should conform to BLM 'Specifications for Descriptions of Tracts of Land'; documents shall be typewritten on paper approx. 8×13 inches with specified margins and double-spaced except for quotations, tabulations, and land descriptions. Proclamations shall conclude with the prescribed recitation wording ('IN WITNESS WHEREOF...').

rubrics_metrics.name: Routing and approval of drafts for Executive orders and proclamations (§19.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: A proposed Executive order or proclamation shall be submitted, with seven copies, first to the Director of the Office of Management and Budget with a letter signed by the head or authorized officer of the originating agency explaining the nature, purpose, background, effect, and relation to laws and other orders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If OMB approves, it transmits to the Attorney General for consideration as to form and legality. If Attorney General approves, it transmits to the Director of the Office of the Federal Register (or, in urgent cases, directly to the President). The OFR Director, after ensuring conformity to §19.1 and freedom from typographical/clerical error, transmits the document and three copies to the President. Disapproval by OMB or the Attorney General requires presentation with a statement of reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Routing and certification of originals and copies for signed Executive orders/proclamations (§19.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the order or proclamation is signed by the President, the original and two copies shall be forwarded to the Director of the Federal Register for publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office of the Federal Register shall place the notation 'Certified to be a true copy of the original' on the copies, to be signed by the Director or authorized person.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proclamations for observance of special days or events (§19.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Responsibility for preparation and presentation of proposed proclamations calling for observance of special days or events shall be assigned by the Director of OMB to appropriate agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such proposed proclamations shall be submitted at least 60 days before the date of the specified observance. The Director of OMB shall transmit approved commemorative proclamations to the President.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of treaties and international agreements (§19.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: These regulations do not apply to treaties, conventions, protocols, or other international agreements, or proclamations thereof by the President, consistent with 44 U.S.C. 1511.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'Presidential proclamations and Executive orders' (§19.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: The term includes such attachments referred to in the respective proclamations or orders, except as the President or his representative may otherwise direct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liaison officers for the U.S. Government Manual (§20.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each specified entity (legislative & judicial branch agencies, executive agencies without §16.1 liaison or wishing a separate Manual liaison, quasi-official agencies, or other agencies the Director believes should be included) shall appoint an officer to maintain liaison with the Office on Manual matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each liaison officer will ensure agency compliance with part 9 and part 20 of the chapter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation of agency statements for the Government Manual (§20.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall submit for publication in the Manual an official draft of information required by §9.2 and part 20 in accordance with schedules established under §20.7.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organization requirements for Manual statements (§20.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Information on lines of authority and organization may be reflected in a chart if the chart clearly delineates organizational structure and is perfectly legible when reduced to Manual page size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Charts not meeting legibility requirements will not be included. Listings of heads of operating units should reflect relationships between units. Narrative descriptions duplicating charts or lists will not be published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description of program activities for Manual statements (§20.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Descriptions should clearly state the public purposes the agency serves and the programs that carry out those purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Descriptions of responsibilities common to most agencies will not be accepted for publication in the Manual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sources of information in Manual statements (§20.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide pertinent sources of information useful to the public (employment, consumer activities, contracts, services to small business, etc.) with each agency statement, plainly identifying places where the public may obtain information or make submittals or requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form, style, arrangement, and apportionment for Manual statements (§20.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director of the Federal Register determines the form, style, arrangement, and apportionment of space for agency statements and other Manual materials, using the U.S. Government Printing Office Style Manual as the applicable reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manual deadline dates and consequences (§20.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must comply with deadline dates established by the Director for transmittal of statements and verification of proofs to provide timely public information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to comply may result in publication of an outdated statement or omission of material, depriving the public of expected information in that edition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drafting documents subject to codification (§21.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency that prepares a document subject to codification shall draft it as an amendment to the Code of Federal Regulations in accordance with this subchapter before submitting it to the Office of the Federal Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each such document shall include words of issuance and amendatory language that precisely describe the relationship of the new provisions to the Code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of expiration of codified material (§21.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever a codified regulation expires after a specified period by its own terms or by law, the issuing agency shall submit a notification by document for publication in the FEDERAL REGISTER.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code structure rules: titles, subtitles, chapters, subchapters, parts, subparts, sections (§21.7-21.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Titles are major divisions of the Code grouping broadly related government functions. Subtitles may distinguish materials from an agency's components. Chapters are normal divisions of a title assigned to agencies and subject matter; subchapters may group related parts. Parts are unified bodies of regulations applying to specific functions; subparts and undesignated center heads may group related sections. Sections are the normal subdivisions within parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter and subchapter assignments are made by the Office of the Federal Register after agency consultation.
